samples.summary: Drag-move (`moveRangeTo`) bypasses the new freeze-pane merge guard

mergedFrom.evidence: `Sheet.setFreezePane` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:513-517) writes the freeze position without inspecting `this.merges`, and the freeze-handle drag reaches it directly (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:2972-2974, and the toggle at 1382-1389). Dropping the freeze line through the middle of an existing merged block yields the same straddling block the delta's `crossesFreezePane` guard now refuses to create by paste, so the invariant the paste guard (and the renderer) relies on is still reachable from another entry point. verdict.reason: The freeze-pane merge guard is real and enforced only on the paste path: sheet.ts:2416-2424 refuses with 'merge-paste-frozen' via crossesFreezePane (sheet.ts:2491-2501), and canMergeSelection applies the same rule at sheet.ts:4653. moveRangeTo pre-flights only merge-source-split (sheet.ts:2658-2662) and merge-dest-partial (sheet.ts:2664-2670), then re-creates moved blocks at translated anchors with a raw this.store.setMerge at sheet.ts:2749-2755 — no freeze-pane check, and store.setMerge (store/memory.ts:586) does not add one. The path is reachable from the UI: startCellDragMove (view/worksheet.ts:4230) computes the drop ref from the mouse with no frozen-pane restriction (view/worksheet.ts:4248, 4336) and calls sheet.moveRangeTo at view/worksheet.ts:4350, so dragging a merged block onto/over the frozen boundary creates exactly the straddling block paste and the merge button both refuse. Guard bypass via an unguarded second entry point is precisely this lens's lane; no counter-guard found.

mergedFrom.summary: A refused `merge-paste-partial` paste still loses the user's cut/copy buffer, because the view clears it unconditionally after `paste()` returns

finding.summary: Both view paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally right after `sheet.paste(...)`, so the new merge propagation only ever runs on the FIRST paste after a copy
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4937-4938 `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer();` and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:724-725 do the same. `Sheet.paste` only takes the internal branch when `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2233). Once the view has cleared the buffer, a second Ctrl+V of the same clipboard content falls through to the plain-TSV branch (sheet.ts:2290), which carries no merges and is explicitly exempt from the new plan/refuse logic. The user-visible consequence is precisely the bug this change fixes: the 2nd and later pastes re-introduce the 'values written into cells hidden under a destination merge, resurfacing on unmerge' behaviour, and `merge-paste-partial` never fires. The new unit tests drive `Sheet` directly and never call `clearCopyBuffer`, so nothing in the suite covers the real app sequence. Fix likely belongs at the two view call sites (only clear on cut, or clear only when the paste actually consumed the buffer).

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: worksheet.ts:4939-4940 and spreadsheet.ts:724-725 both call clearCopyBuffer() unconditionally immediately after sheet.paste(), and clearCopyBuffer sets copyBuffer = undefined (sheet.ts:2139-2141). Sheet.paste's internal branch — the only branch containing the new merge plan/refusal logic (sheet.ts:2249-2266) — is gated on `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text` (sheet.ts:2234). The only writes to copyBuffer are in copy() (2154) and cut() (2175), so nothing restores it; a second paste of the same clipboard content deterministically falls through to the plain-TSV branch (sheet.ts:2283-2286), which carries no merge metadata and is exempt from refusal. The Ctrl+V path is reachable (worksheet.ts:5136) and Spreadsheet.paste() is a public API. No guard, caller, or restoration path refutes it; the task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260912-...-todo.md:45-49) notes the unconditional clear only for the cut/refusal case, not for repeat pastes, and the external-paste non-goal does not cover a repeated internal copy-paste. In-lane for blast radius (behaviour of an exported symbol whose external call sites defeat the new logic) and major by impact: the 2nd+ paste re-introduces values written under a destination merge and merge-paste-partial never fires.

mergedFrom.summary: Merges created by `applyPasteMerges` bypass `canMergeSelection`'s frozen-pane constraint, which every interactive merge path honours

finding.summary: Paste-created merges bypass the freeze-pane guard that every other merge-creation path honours, violating the invariant documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253 and assumed by the renderer
finding.evidence: The only existing merge-creation entry point, `mergeSelection`, refuses a block crossing the freeze boundary via `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4591-4599: `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols`). `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253` states "Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed." The new `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2390) translates the copied blocks by the paste delta and creates them with no freeze check, so with `frozenCols=2` copying a merged D1:E1 and pasting at B1 yields a B1:C1 block straddling the boundary. The renderer relies on the invariant: `packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1917` `toCellRect` computes the merged rect from a single scrolled origin, so a straddling block is drawn with the wrong rect across the frozen pane (the same hole exists in `moveRangeTo`, which is also unguarded, but this change adds a second reachable path). Fix belongs in `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new `planPasteMerges` translates copied merge blocks by the paste delta "with no freeze check". The code contradicts this: sheet.ts:2416-2424 explicitly tests every translated block with `this.crossesFreezePane(toMergeRange(m.anchor, m.span))` and returns `{ ok: false, refusal: 'merge-paste-frozen' }`. The caller refuses before any mutation at sheet.ts:2261-2264 (`if (!plan.ok) { this.refuse(plan.refusal); return; }`), so `applyPasteMerges` never sees a straddling block. The guard is the shared helper `crossesFreezePane` (sheet.ts:2491-2501), the same one `canMergeSelection` uses (sheet.ts:4653) — so the invariant is enforced by one rule, not bypassed. The finding's quoted evidence also does not match the source: it cites `sheet.ts:4591-4599` with inline `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols`, which does not exist at that location. The refusal is fully plumbed (`RangeOpRefusal` at sheet.ts:232, UI notice at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:112), documented (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:109-112), and directly tested for the exact described scenario at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:621-646. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: Split-refusal is now suppressed based on a stale copy-buffer snapshot; nothing invalidates copyBuffer.merges between cut and paste
finding.evidence: The new `travelling` set is built from `this.copyBuffer.merges` (sheet.ts:2431-2437), a snapshot taken at cut time. `copyBuffer` is only ever cleared explicitly (sheet.ts:2138-2140, 2284) — `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4679-4713), `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4658) and the row/column structural ops (sheet.ts:1245, 1253) never invalidate or re-map it. So after a cut, a user (or a remote collaborator over yorkie-store) can unmerge/re-merge so that a block currently anchored at a stale source anchor spans into the destination region; that block is then excluded from the `isRangeInRange` split check even though it is a live destination block, and it is instead deleted wholesale by the cut branch's `replacedMerges` push (sheet.ts:2276-2282) using the stale span. A refusal the guard is supposed to raise is skipped and a destination block disappears silently. To confirm: exercise cut → unmerge/merge at the same anchor with a wider span → paste at an overlapping destination. Fix belongs on the new code (validate travelling anchors against the current merge map, or invalidate the copy buffer on merge-map changes).

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `travelling` is built straight from the stale `copyBuffer.merges` snapshot with no validation against the live merge map. The code does the opposite: `sheet.ts:2431` routes the snapshot through `this.liveMergesAmong(sourceMerges)`, and `liveMergesAmong` (sheet.ts:2478-2485) keeps only entries whose anchor is present in the live `this.merges` map AND whose span matches exactly (`live.rs === m.span.rs && live.cs === m.span.cs`). `travelling` (sheet.ts:2450) is derived solely from that validated list, so any block that was unmerged, or re-merged at the same anchor with a different/wider span, is NOT in `travelling`, stays in `replaced` (sheet.ts:2451-2453), fails `isRangeInRange(m.range, destRange)` and triggers the `merge-paste-partial` refusal (sheet.ts:2454-2456) — precisely the refusal the finding says is skipped. `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4702) and `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4741) mutate the same `this.merges` map that `liveMergesAmong` reads, so mid-cut edits are visible to the check; invalidating the copy buffer is unnecessary because the anchor+span identity check subsumes it. The finding's other cited evidence is also absent: sheet.ts:2268-2278 (the cut branch) contains no `replacedMerges` push at all — it only sets `isCut`, `cutSourceRange`, `cutRefMap` and clears `copyBuffer`. The proposed fix ("validate travelling anchors against the current merge map") is already implemented.
